instructions: Fill a large pot with water and bring it to a boil. Cook the rice noodles following the package, drain and rinse under cold water. Divide them among 4 bowls.
Meanwhile, cut the squid into rings and halve the fish balls. Cube the tofu. Chop the bok choy into 1 inch pieces. Mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the fermented tofu and mash it into the oil with the back of a spoon. Add the soybean paste and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, fish sauce, sugar and rice vinegar. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the fish balls and tofu and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the shrimp and squid and cook for 2 minutes, until the shrimp are pink and the squid is opaque. Don't cook them longer or the squid turns rubbery.
Add the bok choy and bean sprouts and cook for 1 minute.
Ladle the soup over the noodles. Chop a handful of cilantro and sprinkle it on top. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Hot Thai Kitchen's yen ta fo (the most-rated version) and Simply Suwanee couldn't be read, so the lead is Travel Food Atlas, which has no ratings. It builds the pink broth from fermented red tofu and soybean paste with garlic, fish sauce, sugar and vinegar, then cooks fish balls, shrimp, squid and tofu in it. Broth is raised from 4 to 5 cups so the bowls are soupy, baby bok choy replaces water spinach, and the red food coloring is left out. Cooking the noodles separately keeps the broth clear.
